newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: "Be humble, be honest" Goh tells Singapore MPs.
newsitem.headline: "Be humble, be honest" Goh tells Singapore MPs.

text.p: Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong has told his party's victorious parliamentary candidates to be honest, humble and start working to win the next general election immediately.
"Victory must not go to our heads," he told his People's Action Party (PAP) members of parliament who now fill all but two of the assembly's 83 seats after last week's elections.
"The responsibilities we have to shoulder require us to be humble, not arrogant," Goh said in written "Rules of Prudence".
"Start working now for the next general elections in 2002," he said, adding that MPs should make sure the party's campaign promises were implemented.
The bulk of the 22-paragraph set of rules were about honesty.
"I cannot stress too strongly that every MP must be seen to be beyond the influence of gifts or favours," he said.

PAP members would have to disclose their incomes to Goh within two weeks, hand over all gifts to a top party official, except those from relatives and close friends, and pay up if they wanted to keep them.
Nor would any lobbying be tolerated, Goh said. "To be above board, all communications with public officers must be in writing and on the record," he wrote.
"I am releasing a copy of this letter to the media so that the public knows the high standards we demand of our MPs," he said.
Goh also told MPs to "bring into the open the malicious and the spurious talk in the coffee shops, hawker centres and among some taxi drivers whenever we can pin them down".

But, he added: "You must, however, exercise discretion when putting your points across. Never kick the ball into our own goal. Bring out the grapevine talk for the government to rebut, not unwittingly to add to the malicious but baseless gossip."
The PAP was guaranteed a majority before a vote was cast in the January 2 election when the opposition decided to contest only 36 of the 83 seats.
It won all but two of the contested seats with a 65 percent share of the vote.
